name: Square-Free Edges of Ample Families Are Bridges
statement: Every cycle in the one-inclusion graph of an ample family, viewed as an edge chain over $\mathbb F_2$, is a sum of boundaries of contained squares. Consequently every edge that belongs to no contained square is a bridge.
proof: Induct on the active coordinates. Pair the edges of a cycle in a chosen direction. The projected endpoints lie in the ample and therefore connected intersection of the two sections; paths between each pair lift to square ladders whose boundaries cancel those directional edges. What remains is a sum of cycles inside the two ample sections, handled inductively. An edge on a graph cycle has coefficient one in that cycle, while every square-boundary sum has coefficient zero on an edge lying in no square, proving the bridge claim.
